crossRefs.note: Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried to his god. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea…
Then the men feared Yahweh exceedingly; and they offered a sacrifice to Yahweh, and made vows.
Then they cry to Yahweh in their trouble, and he brings them out of their distress.
Yahweh, in trouble they have visited you. They poured out a prayer when your chastening was on them.
Whoever sheds man’s blood, his blood will be shed by man, for God made man in his own image.
Forgive, Yahweh, your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, and don’t allow innocent blood among your people Israel.”…
When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer…
But our God is in the heavens. He does whatever he pleases.
Whatever Yahweh pleased, that he has done, in heaven and in earth, in the seas and in all deeps.

translations.web: Therefore they cried to Yahweh, and said, “We beg you, Yahweh, we beg you, don’t let us die for this man’s life, and don’t lay on us innocent blood; for you, Yahweh, have done as it pleased you.”
translations.bsb: So they cried out to the LORD: “Please, O LORD, do not let us perish on account of this man’s life! Do not charge us with innocent blood! For You, O LORD, have done as You pleased.”
translations.kjv: Wherefore they cried unto the LORD, and said, We beseech thee, O LORD, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O LORD, hast done as it pleased
translations.asv: Wherefore they cried unto Jehovah, and said, We beseech thee, O Jehovah, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood; for thou, O Jehovah, hast done as it pleased thee.
